# Implementation Plan: Manual-Grounded Knowledge Base and Candidate-Constrained Planning

**Branch**: `004-manual-grounded-planning` | **Date**: 2026-11-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/004-manual-grounded-planning/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan was generated by `/speckit.plan`. Phase 0 research is in [research.md](./research.md); Phase 1 data and interface contracts are in [data-model.md](./data-model.md), [contracts/](./contracts/), and [quickstart.md](./quickstart.md).

## Summary

Feature 004 upgrades the documentation substrate and adds an opt-in planning stage, without changing the Gate 3 semantic oracle or the two-tier repair contract.

1. **Step A (MVP, `--pipeline manual-kb`)**: replace the online GRASS 8.6 scraper with a strictly offline GRASS 8.5 ingestion pipeline; store complete manual sections, flags, closed enums, and provenance; render compact `ManualCard`s within a deterministic token budget; synthesize API flag kwargs; enforce closed-enum checks only in the new modes; and preserve underlying `ERROR:`/`Legal range:` lines in repair prompts.
2. **Step B (`--pipeline planned`)**: retrieve an up-to-12-module shortlist with `shortlist_k=12` (minimum eight when available; all available with a recorded shortfall otherwise), ask a local model for a JSON plan using only those candidates, validate the plan against the knowledge base, retrieve per-step manual cards plus functional alternatives, and synthesize with the manual as the authority over the plan. Invalid plans or timeouts fall back to manual-kb after one pre-execution repair; tool swaps or one constrained re-plan consume the producing repair tier, with total planner invocations capped at three.
3. **Governance first**: the constitution is amended to `v1.4.0` (2026-11-19), ratifying Feature 004, internal JSON planning, and the 14B/32B benchmark models while retaining 7B as the baseline and 3B as smoke-only.
4. **Isolation and evidence**: `legacy` remains the default; `pipeline`, `num_ctx`, and the manual budget are part of `ResumeKey`, `Attempt`, and `RunSummary`; reports expose per-mode `Pass@Executed`/`Pass@Semantic` comparisons; a socket audit proves zero outbound calls.

The design deliberately preserves `format_context()`, `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, the 394-test baseline, the `1 + static_limit + runtime_limit` candidate bound, SHA-256 byte/AST duplicate rejection, and report-only semantic failures.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Python 3.11+; repository virtual environment runs Python 3.13

**Primary Dependencies**: Python standard library (`argparse`, `json`, `sqlite3`, `dataclasses`, `pathlib`, `subprocess`, `hashlib`, `ast`), `sqlite-vec`, `beautifulsoup4` for HTML fallback, `ollama` client, `pytest`, local GRASS 8.5.0 CLI, local GRASS Markdown/HTML documentation. No new network dependency is introduced.

**Storage**: Additive SQLite knowledge base at `data/grass_knowledge.db`; JSON per-case results and `run_summary.json`; existing benchmark artifacts. Full manual sections are stored at rest; inference renders compact cards. Commit the DB only when it is at most 50 MB; otherwise generate it during setup and commit the build report and checksums.

**Testing**: `pytest`; 394 existing tests are the zero-regression baseline; new unit tests use checked-in Markdown/XML/HTML fixtures; live-GRASS tests remain `slow` and skippable.

**Target Platform**: Linux headless host with a local GRASS 8.5.0 installation, a provisioned North Carolina dataset, and local Ollama. No cloud API and no network access.

**Project Type**: CLI benchmark harness plus importable Python library; no new service or package layout.

**Performance Goals**: Default 8,192-token context with a 45% manual documentation budget (~3,686 tokens); 16,384 tokens available as an explicit opt-in with the same policy; zero context overflow or silent truncation; pilot wall-clock P95 within 2× a matched legacy baseline; at most three planner invocations per case (initial plan, one plan repair, one constrained re-plan) plus synthesis.

**Constraints**: Fully offline; `--pipeline legacy` remains the default and behaviorally unchanged; all 394 existing tests pass; no changes to the two-tier budgets, duplicate detection, `PERMANENT` isolation, or report-only semantic failures; no semantic-repair tier; no cloud model; total planner invocations capped at three.

**Scale/Scope**: 738 local Markdown manuals and 728 HTML manuals on the reference host; 543 tools in the current DB; 10-case semantic pilot and 40-case benchmark; 3 pipeline modes; 3 approved benchmark models; at most 5 plan steps and an up-to-12-module shortlist (`shortlist_k=12`, minimum eight when available).

### Post-Design Re-check

- The planner reads only a candidate shortlist and cannot invent tools; its output is validated before use.
- Full manuals are stored at rest but never dumped unbounded into the prompt; a hard budget and fail-closed rule protect context.
- Strict enum validation is gated to `manual-kb`/`planned`; default legacy validation remains byte-for-byte compatible, and the explicit legacy-only `--strict-options` opt-in is off by default.
- No semantic repair is introduced; Gate 3 remains report-only.
- No new network path exists.
- Build-time tooling may invoke `grass --config path` and `grass.script.task.get_interface_description`; Principle II's `grass.tools`-only rule governs generated scripts, not the offline ingestion builder.

## Phase 2: Step A — Local Manual KB MVP (`--pipeline manual-kb`)

**Goal**: Make Step A independently runnable and testable before any planner work.

### 2.1 Local source and ingestion

1. `kb_source.py`:
   - Resolve `GISBASE` from `$GISBASE` or `grass --config path`.
   - Enumerate modules from `$GISBASE/docs/mkdocs/source/*.md`; fall back to `$GISBASE/docs/html/*.html`, then installed module names.
   - Run `--interface-description` XML in a temporary local GRASS session. Prefer `grass.script.task.get_interface_description`; accept `--dataset-project`; when no project is supplied, use a minimal local project. If XML still cannot be obtained, manifest modules fail the build (exit `3`); optional/add-on modules log a warning, are ingested from local Markdown when available with `xml_validated=false`, and are reported/skipped only when no Markdown exists.
   - Return a deterministic, sorted module inventory with source paths and hashes.

2. `kb_parse.py`:
   - Parse Markdown front matter, `grass.tools.Tools.<name>` signature, Python parameter types, defaults, `DESCRIPTION`, `NOTES`, `EXAMPLES`.
   - Deduplicate the Command-line / `grass.tools` / `grass.script` tabs; store one canonical section per heading.
   - Parse XML flags, parameters, defaults, `multiple`, `<values>` with descriptions, and generic flags.
   - Merge by parameter name, using the Markdown signature for API names. Persist mismatches in `source_mismatches_json` and summarize them in the build report; never silently drop them.
   - Set `xml_validated=true` when XML enrichment is applied and `false` for Markdown-only optional/add-on records.
   - Synthesize `flags`, `overwrite`, `verbose`, `quiet`, `superquiet` into the API parameter map.
   - Mark closed enums only when `<values>` is genuinely finite; exclude ranges, free text, map names, and file paths.

3. `kb_schema.py`:
   - Preserve `tools` and `tools_vec`.
   - Add `flags_json`, `options_json`, `source`, `grass_version`, `content_hash`, `source_mismatches_json`, and `xml_validated` to `tools`.
   - Add `tool_flags`, `tool_options`, `tool_sections`, `db_meta`.
   - Use an explicit schema-version row in `db_meta`; migration is idempotent and additive.
   - Store token estimates per section and content hashes for provenance.

4. `scripts/build_knowledge_base.py`:
   - Remove `requests` and all network calls.
   - Add `--gisbase`, `--db`, `--strict`, `--partial`, `--dataset-project`, `--rebuild`, `--source local`, `--report`.
   - Read the checked-in `benchmarks/kb_required_modules.txt` manifest; fail with exit `3` if the manifest is missing or any listed module lacks a manual.
   - Default partial policy: ingest optional/add-on modules from Markdown when XML is unavailable (`xml_validated=false`), skip them only when no Markdown exists, and fail if any manifest module is missing.
   - Exit non-zero with a named module on a strict-build omission.
   - Commit the rebuilt DB only when it is at most 50 MB; otherwise generate it during setup and commit the build report and checksums.

### 2.2 Retriever and ManualCard

1. Extend `ToolDoc` with optional `flags`, `options`, `sections`, `source`, `grass_version`, `content_hash`, `source_mismatches`, and `xml_validated` at the end; defaults preserve positional construction.
2. Add `GrassToolsRetriever.get_manual(name)` and a tolerant row mapper that works with old DBs.
3. Add `TOOL_FAMILIES` beside `STEP_SYNONYMS`:
   - reclassify: `r.reclass`, `r.recode`, `r.mapcalc`
   - clean: `v.clean`, `v.edit`, `v.generalize`
   - buffer: `v.buffer`, `r.buffer`
   - import: `v.import`, `r.import`, `v.in.ogr`, `r.in.gdal`
   - rasterize: `v.to.rast`, `r.mapcalc`
   - extend as needed from the local module inventory.
   This must land before `manual_context.py` so US1 cards can include alternatives.
4. `manual_context.py`:
   - `ManualCard` dataclass with tool, signature, flags, parameters, constraints, examples, alternatives, omissions, token estimate.
   - Budget = `int(num_ctx * 0.45)`, default `num_ctx=8192`.
   - Token estimate = conservative `ceil(chars / 3.5)` plus a 10% safety margin; record actual `prompt_eval_count` after the call.
   - Per-card target = 250-600 tokens at 8K; report every estimate, and allow an out-of-range card only when required flags, enums, or constraints explain it.
   - Render order: signature → flags → parameters/types/defaults/closed enums → top-3 NOTES constraints → 1-2 examples → alternatives.
   - The API signature, flags, and closed enums are mandatory and strictly fail-closed; only optional prose (`DESCRIPTION`, secondary `EXAMPLES`) may be listed in `omissions`.
   - Apply the deterministic compaction order (deduplicate tools, compact alternatives to one, drop optional prose) before raising a named budget error. Never silently truncate mandatory sections.
   - Deduplicate by tool name across steps.

### 2.3 Static validation and healing diagnostics

1. `validate_api()` gains an optional `strict_options: bool = False`; existing callers and tests keep the old behavior.
2. In `manual-kb` and `planned`, validate:
   - flag characters against known module/generic flags;
   - closed-enum parameters against stored options;
   - list-valued enums by splitting on commas;
   - never validate free text, map names, ranges, or file paths.
3. `GrassCodeGenerator` and `static_guard()` pass the pipeline mode/strict flag. `legacy` passes its resolved opt-in value (default `False`).
4. `error_excerpt()`:
   - If the trailing exception is a wrapper `ToolError`, prefer the last underlying `ERROR:` line and append its continuation lines, including `Legal range:`, `options:`, or `Allowed values:`.
   - Return a verbatim substring; keep the existing 400-character cap or raise it only with a bounded multi-line policy.
5. `Healer.parameter_list()`:
   - Include module flags and allowed enum values in the parameter table.
   - Keep deterministic ordering and the existing `None` behavior for unknown tools.

### 2.4 Manual-kb pipeline wiring

1. Add `pipeline: str = "legacy"` to `GenerationConfig` and `ExecutionConfig`; add `num_ctx: int = 8192`, `manual_context_tokens: int | None = None`, `strict_options: bool = False`, `shortlist_k: int = 12` (must be between `8` and `12`; `rag_top_k=5` remains unchanged), and `planner_timeout: int = 60`.
2. `GrassCodeGenerator.generate()` dispatches:
   - `legacy`: existing exactly;
   - `manual-kb`: retrieve top-k, render manual cards, use the existing zero-chat synthesis and extractor.
3. `Healer` optionally receives a manual renderer and the pipeline mode; repair docs use cards when not legacy.
4. `run_gate2`/`run_gate3` expose the mode and context flags; pass them into generation, static guards, and healing, and record the resolved mode/context/budget on the attempt and run summary (FR-016).
5. Tests and checkpoint: `pytest -q` remains 394 green; the three pilot failures are covered by unit tests; a manual-kb pilot run is possible end-to-end.

## Phase 3: Step B — Candidate-Constrained Planning (`--pipeline planned`)

**Goal**: Add planning only after the manual-kb MVP is independently validated.

### 3.1 Shortlist and planner

1. `Shortlist` = existing hybrid retrieval using `shortlist_k=12` (legacy/manual-kb `rag_top_k=5` unchanged), with the current anti-crowding and wrapper rules. Provide at least eight real modules when available. If fewer than eight are available, use all of them and record `shortlist_shortfall`; if none are available, fall back to manual-kb.
2. `planner.py`:
   - Build a prompt containing the task, inventory summary, and candidate names with one-line descriptions.
   - Require JSON only, with exactly: `steps[]`, `assumptions[]`.
   - Each step: `id`, `intent`, `tool`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `output_types`, `constraints`.
   - Maximum 5 steps; one tool per step; tools only from the shortlist.
3. `ExecutionPlan` validation:
   - tool exists in the KB;
   - raster/vector type compatibility;
   - output names distinct and non-empty;
   - inputs are inventory maps or prior-step outputs;
   - no step uses a tool outside the shortlist;
   - max 5 steps.
4. Invalid JSON/empty plan/validation failure/timeout:
   - one pre-execution plan repair with the error and the same shortlist;
   - the planner timeout defaults to 60 seconds and is configurable;
   - if still invalid, fall back to manual-kb single-shot; no static/runtime tier is charged; no extra candidate.
5. Store the plan, its revision, the plan-repair count, and the constrained re-plan count in attempt evidence; never emit it to the final script.

### 3.2 Per-step retrieval and synthesis

1. For each step, exact lookup of the primary tool plus 1-2 alternatives from `TOOL_FAMILIES`.
2. Render deduplicated cards within the global manual budget. If the budget is exceeded, apply the deterministic compaction order: (1) deduplicate repeated tools across steps, (2) compact alternatives to one per step, (3) drop optional `EXAMPLES`/`DESCRIPTION` prose while keeping signatures, flags, closed enums, and the top-3 `NOTES` constraints, then (4) fail closed only if mandatory sections still exceed the budget.
3. `agentic.py` orchestrates: shortlist → plan → cards → synthesis.
4. Add `AGENTIC_SYSTEM_PROMPT` = existing `SYSTEM_PROMPT` plus:
   - the plan is advisory; the manual card is authoritative;
   - substitute a documented alternative if the primary tool cannot satisfy the step;
   - use flags/options exactly as documented;
   - file-based parameters must be created before the call;
   - final output remains executable code only.
5. `GrassCodeGenerator.generate()` dispatches to `agentic.py` for `planned`; `last_*` debug fields remain populated.

### 3.3 Repair escalation

1. Same-tool manual card for the failing tool.
2. Parameter/option pivot with flags and closed enums.
3. Tool swap: retrieve alternatives for the failing functional step; prompt explicitly excludes the failed tool.
4. One constrained re-plan per case after a failed execution: planner sees original prompt, failed plan, error, and alternatives; then synthesize. This is distinct from the pre-execution plan repair; both may occur, but total planner invocations are capped at three.
5. Charge the producing tier; keep the `1 + static_limit + runtime_limit` bound; planner fallback never charges a tier.
6. Preserve byte/AST no-op detection, history rendering, and the semantic report-only rule.

### 3.4 Checkpoint

`--pipeline planned` runs a multi-step pilot, invalid plans fall back, a wrong primary tool can be substituted, and the legacy/manual-kb tests remain green.

## Phase 4: Isolation, Reporting, and Offline Assurance

1. Add `pipeline` (`legacy` | `manual-kb` | `planned`), `num_ctx`, and the resolved manual budget to `ResumeKey`; include them in `matches()`.
2. Add `pipeline`, `num_ctx`, manual budget, and plan/tool-swap diagnostics to `Attempt`; add `pipeline`, `num_ctx`, manual budget, plan repair/fallback/replan/shortfall counters, and context-overflow evidence to `RunSummary` and `run_summary.json`.
3. Keep `case_result.json` at `schema_version: 1`; all new fields are additive with defaults.
4. `reporting.py`:
   - show the pipeline mode in the header;
   - add a per-mode ablation table (plan repairs, fallbacks, re-plans, shortfalls, tool swaps, P95) when summaries from multiple modes are supplied;
   - add `render_pipeline_ablation()` and a `--report-only --ablation-dirs <dirs>` path that reads each run summary and refuses duplicate modes;
   - keep the Gate 3 oracle and metrics unchanged.
5. Preflight:
   - in `manual-kb`/`planned`, require the new schema, a matching `grass_version`, and the required provenance (`source`, `built_at`, `content_hash`, and `$GISBASE` presence); exit `3` with a rebuild hint on mismatch or missing provenance;
   - in `legacy`, accept the old DB and old validation behavior.
6. Socket audit:
   - add a test/audit that records every outbound `socket.connect` during a local KB build and a benchmark case;
   - assert zero external connections.
7. Tests: pipeline isolation, resume mismatch, report ablation, provenance mismatch (`tests/test_preflight_provenance.py`), offline audit, 394-test regression.

## Phase 5: Evaluation and Polish

1. Run the full suite: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`; 394 existing plus new tests.
2. Run Step A pilot: `--pipeline manual-kb` at 32B with at least 3 seeds; 7B/14B are optional comparisons and 3B is a smoke check. Evaluate SC-003/SC-004 at 32B.
3. Run Step B pilot: `--pipeline planned` at 32B with at least 3 seeds; use the same optional comparisons.
4. Run the 40-case suite for the strongest configuration.
5. Measure the legacy baseline on the same host, dataset, model, case set, and seed count; assert the new modes' P95 is at most 2x that baseline.
6. Compare:
   - `Pass@Executed`, `Pass@Semantic`, `Pass@1`, `Pass@Healed`;
   - per-case verdicts for `pilot_tc_08`, `pilot_tc_14`, `pilot_tc_32`;
   - plan validity/fallback rate, tool swaps, manual-card tokens, truncation/overflow events;
   - prompt/completion tokens, P95 latency, tier usage, duplicates.
7. Update `quickstart.md`, the Gate 3 report, and any operator documentation.

## Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Local Markdown absent or incomplete | XML + HTML fallback; record source kind/provenance; strict/partial build policy |
| Markdown/XML parameter-name mismatch | Signature authoritative for API names; persist in `source_mismatches_json` and the build report; never drop options silently |
| 8K context overflow | 45% card budget; deterministic priority; fail closed; record actual prompt tokens |
| Planner hallucinates or picks wrong tool | `shortlist_k=12` candidate shortlist (minimum eight when available; shortfall recorded); KB validation; alternatives; manual authoritative; one plan repair then fallback |
| Planner locks in `r.reclass` for float input | Manual notes expose integer constraint; `r.recode`/`r.mapcalc` alternatives; tool swap in repair |
| Legacy regression | `legacy` default; strict enum checks gated; `format_context()`/`SYSTEM_PROMPT` unchanged; 394-test gate |
| Repair prompt hides the real error | Preserve underlying `ERROR:`/legal-range lines; options in parameter table |
| No-op/budget drift | Existing byte/AST detector and tier accounting unchanged; plan changes cannot bypass code duplicate checks |
| DB growth or distribution | Full text stored at rest; commit at most 50 MB, otherwise generate during setup and commit report/checksums |
| Report mixes modes | `pipeline` in resume key, attempt, and run summary; report header/ablation table |
| Benchmark overfitting | 3 seeds, 40-case suite, held-out regression cases; no tuning on pilot ids only |

## Complexity Tracking

| Added Complexity | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|
| New `kb_source`/`kb_parse`/`kb_schema` modules | Local Markdown/XML/HTML parsing, provenance, and additive migration are distinct responsibilities | A single 1,000-line builder script would be harder to test offline and to keep deterministic |
| Full manual sections at rest plus compact cards | Completeness for provenance/retrieval, but bounded context for 8K models | Storing only cards would lose NOTES/EXAMPLES needed for `tc_32`; dumping full manuals overflows |
| Planner plus shortlist and validation | Multi-step ordering and tool arbitration without hallucinated modules | A free-form planner over 543 modules is unvalidatable; a retrieval-only pipeline leaves multi-step ordering unresolved |
| Strict enum validation gated by mode | Safety in new modes without changing legacy behavior | Applying it globally violates the zero-regression contract |
| Pipeline metadata in three records | Resume isolation and credible ablation evidence | A single run-level flag cannot prevent mixed resumes or per-case attribution |
| Additional model stack entries | Benchmark comparison at 14B/32B | Keeping only 7B/3B contradicts the pilot evidence and the feature scope |
